role: URL parsing, literal address guards, and mixed Arabic/share extraction

scope.method: Read-only static review; no builds, tests, emulator, device, or network requests were run. Findings are demonstrated by exact string/control-flow traces.

findings.title: Closing prose punctuation is included in shared URL
findings.certainty: Confirmed by regex and downstream string flow; not device-reproduced
findings.evidence: The regex terminates only at whitespace, angle brackets, or a double quote. For the ordinary mixed Arabic share text 'شاهد (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=abc123)' it extracts 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=abc123)' instead of the enclosed link. URI accepts the closing parenthesis as query content, so url() preserves it. An Arabic sentence comma similarly produces 'https://example.com/video.mp4%D8%8C' from 'شاهد https://example.com/video.mp4،' because the comma is captured and toASCIIString percent-encodes it. MainViewModel.receive forwards that modified URL through edit() and analyze(); there is no later prose punctuation removal. This changes the requested video ID or file path and causes a valid shared link to fail or address a different resource.
reproduction: Share or paste the text: شاهد (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=abc123)
Safety.shared returns https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=abc123) with the prose closing parenthesis in the query.
Alternatively share: شاهد https://example.com/video.mp4، ; the Arabic comma becomes part of the requested path rather than a sentence delimiter.
findings.recommendation: Use a shared-link tokenizer that handles paired enclosing punctuation and Arabic prose delimiters. Remove only unmatched closing delimiters/prose punctuation after extraction while preserving deliberately balanced or encoded characters within a URL, and cover these share forms in SafetyTest.

findings.title: Accepted uppercase HTTPS schemes fail media extraction
findings.certainty: Confirmed by acceptance and downstream case-sensitive requirement; not device-reproduced
findings.evidence: Safety.shared matches schemes case-insensitively, Safety.url validates u.scheme.lowercase(), but returns u.toASCIIString() without normalizing the original scheme spelling. Thus 'HTTPS://www.youtube.com/watch?v=abc123' remains uppercase through receive(), analyze(), and analyzeSource(). NetworkSettings.requireSource allows it case-insensitively and OkHttp parses it, but when direct analysis sees a normal HTML response and returns null, MediaEngine.request rejects it with the case-sensitive startsWith("https://") requirement. MainViewModel.kt:198 also incorrectly declines the HTTPS extractor fallback on a direct IOException for this same input. A lowercase equivalent enters extraction normally.
reproduction: Paste or share a webpage/media-platform URL with scheme spelling HTTPS:// rather than https://.
Observe that Safety.shared and Safety.url accept the URL and retain the uppercase scheme.
For an HTML response DirectDownloader.analyze returns null; MediaEngine.request then throws before invoking the extractor because startsWith("https://") is false.
findings.recommendation: Normalize the scheme in the canonical accepted URL, or compare the parsed scheme case-insensitively at MediaEngine.request and MainViewModel's fallback gate. Add coverage proving uppercase/mixed-case HTTPS follows the same media extraction path as lowercase.

guard_review.result: No transport bypass established in reviewed paths.
evidence: Safety.url is a syntax check; its acceptance of an address alone was not treated as proof of a network-policy bypass.
DirectDownloader.request checks the actual OkHttp-canonicalized request.url.host with requirePublicLiteral at line 51, and secureClient checks it again in the interceptor at line 301.
The production NetworkSettings.client DNS resolver validates every returned InetAddress with Safety.checkedAddresses; the client also disables system proxy routing and automatic redirects.
PublicProxy validates CONNECT authority and port, checks all resolver results at line 87, and connects to the selected checked InetAddress directly at line 129, avoiding a second hostname resolution.

Literal guards reject abbreviated/integer/leading-zero IPv4 and scoped IPv6; publicAddress applies the IPv4 policy to the supported NAT64 prefix and rejects private/site-local/link-local/loopback, multicast, documentation, and listed transition ranges.

test_gaps: SafetyTest covers Arabic prefix text separated from a link by whitespace, but not Arabic sentence punctuation, parenthesized links, or mixed-case schemes through extractor fallback.
No source changes or build/device/test runs were performed by this reviewer.
